title: Margin of Focus — Playbook & Sprint Notebook
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight sprint-style playbook for protecting my attention and improving outcome velocity. Not a formal OKR doc — think of it as a persistent scratchpad that bridges daily habits and measurable micro-KPIs.

Notes to self (top-line):
- Focus is a scarce resource: treat weekly focus-budget like runway.
- Small, measurable bets > vague intentions.
- Track signals (not just outputs) so I can debug sources of variance.

Weekly cadence (how I run this):
1) Monday morning (30m): set 3 intention slots for the week and timebox them on calendar.
2) Midweek (15m): reality check — did any blockers appear? If yes, add one mitigating action.
3) Friday (20m): quick retro + update micro-KPIs and iteration notes.

Micro-KPIs (tracked values, weekly):
- Deep-focus fraction: percent of day in 90+ minute uninterrupted blocks (baseline: 0.18; target: 0.45).
- Ship count: number of merged PRs or completed demos affecting product experience (baseline: 1/week; target: 2/week for sprints where shipping is priority).
- Interrupt rate: number of ad-hoc meetings or Slack pings that force context switch (baseline: ~12/day; target: <6/day).
- Signal density: proportion of meetings with a clear decision or action assigned (baseline: 0.4; target: 0.75).

How I measure (practical):
- Deep-focus fraction: calendar tags + RescueTime coarse check + manual note on Friday.
- Ship count: GitHub PRs merged with "feature/" or "chore/ship" label + demo link.
- Interrupt rate: quick tally in notes app during day (count interruptions) — messy but fast.
- Signal density: meeting notes checklist (decision? owner? due date?).

Experiment slate (current):
- Timebox 2× 90-min deep blocks per day for 8 working days (start 2026-02-02). Hypothesis: two sustained blocks will raise focus fraction to 0.4.
- Interrupt moat: enforce "no Slack pings between 10:00–12:30" with an automated away message for 2 weeks. Measure interrupt rate and perceived stress.
- Mini-demos: schedule 15m Friday walkthroughs with internal stakeholders to increase feedback speed and reduce long review cycles.

Checklist for a focused sprint day:
- Calendar: block two 90-min "deep" events before lunch and one 60-min after lunch.
- Notifications: DND on desktop and mobile; set Slack status with ETA for responses.
- Micro-goal: write 400–800 words of spec / open 1 PR / finish 1 evaluation calibration.
- Exit triage: at EOD, write 3 one-line notes: what worked, what blocked me, next 90-min focus for tomorrow.

Retrospective template (Friday):
- Wins (what shipped / moved forward).
- Failures / blockers (what repeatedly blocked focus).
- Surprises (unexpected insights or new work).
- Experiments to continue / kill (based on data).
- Commitments for next week (3 intent slots).

Past 6 weeks quick log (high level):
- Week of 2026-01-05: focus fraction ~0.22; shipped small infra patch (PR#1204). Big blocker: on-call interrupts.
- Week of 2026-01-19: introduced 90-min morning block; focus fraction bumped to 0.31 but late meetings still fragmented afternoons.
- Week of 2026-02-02: started two-block experiment; subjective clarity improved. Interrupt rate fell ~20%.

Open questions / unresolved:
- How to enforce interruption policy across team without sounding gatekeeper? (ask Ibrahim for a short blurb to share in team weekly).
- Is focus fraction a reasonable leading indicator for customer-impacting work? Need to compare weeks where focus fraction >0.35 to feature adoption metrics (link to ENG-3421 notes).
- Can I automate interrupt counts using Slack APIs or is manual tallyging okay for now? (technical depth vs time investment).

Personal heuristics (rules I try to follow):
- If a task needs >3 context switches to complete, break into a separate sprint and protect a deep block.
- Never schedule recurring meetings inside my planned primary deep block.
- If shipping is the priority for the week, reduce meeting commitments by 50% proactively.

Quick action items (this week):
- [ ] Draft a 2-paragraph note for team about "interrupt moat" and post to #eng-growth (due: 2026-02-22). (linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284 for example of shipping cadence)
- [ ] Try automated Slack away message via small bot script (P0 test; ask Noelle for bot template).
- [ ] Tag calendar events with "DEEP" keyword so RescueTime/filters can capture them.

Good enough metrics snapshot (2026-02-20):
- Focus fraction: 0.39 (excl. meetings) — trending toward target.
- Ship count (last 2 weeks): 3 merged feature PRs (one major), 2 followups.
- Interrupt rate: 5–7/day during protected windows (improved).

Closing thought (note to future me):
If I can design a week where context switches are the exception rather than the rule, my throughput and enjoyment will both increase. Keep experiments small, measurable, and reversible. 

Appendix / links to related notes:
- effort-economy sprint notes (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/effort-economy-notes
- example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284
- related Jira: ENG-3421 (investigate time-to-first-response on internal reviews)

---
Meta: this file is mostly a running scratchpad. I will prune and move validated experiments to a formal OKR doc if they consistently change outcomes for 3 consecutive sprints.
